annotation.title_clean: Durkheim’s Theory of the Division of Labor and Its Relevance for Socially Responsible Robotics
annotation.title_en: Durkheim’s Theory of the Division of Labor and Its Relevance for Socially Responsible Robotics
annotation.venue: Frontiers in Artificial Intelligence and Applications, Vol. 366: Social Robots in Social Institutions (IOS Press)
annotation.summary_en: Conference paper applying Durkheim's theory of the division of labor to robotics innovation. It uses his three social pathologies (forced division of labor, excessive division of labor, anomie) to analyze the social and ethical impacts of workplace robots on solidarity, and describes a socially responsible innovation approach.
key_provisions_or_claims: Durkheim's three social pathologies provide an interpretive framework for assessing robots' social impacts in the workplace.
Division of labor underpins the shift from mechanical to organic solidarity.
Robots can contribute to forced or excessive division of labor and anomie.
Advocates socially responsible innovation informed by Durkheim's insights.
